=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py:636, 887 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The fixed four-backtick fence can be closed by untrusted command text, allowing Markdown injection into the report and causing `lookup` to parse a truncated command or injected fields.
  WHY: The report renders untrusted session data inside a fixed fence, and the parser makes the same fixed-fence assumption; both reviewers rate this MAJOR.
- .claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py: _file_pending() reported signature skip | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: `_file_pending` skips reported signatures across all sessions, so occurrences from one session can be omitted when another session reports the same pattern.
  WHY: Shared home-directory state can cause `file` to omit occurrences from `filed-state.json`, leaving the operator's count stale.
- .claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py: _report_now() exception handler calling _release_reservation() | severity=high | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: If posting fails and saving the released reservation also fails, the stale on-disk reservation can prevent another immediate report for that session and signature.
  WHY: A subsequent `report-now` sees the pending reservation and skips the report, delaying operator notification until end-of-stage filing.
- .claude/hooks/permission_prompt_logger.py: spawn_reporter() subprocess.Popen call in main() | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The hook spawns a detached child on every PermissionRequest, including attended sessions where the child exits without posting.
  WHY: The child still reads environment and local state before determining the session is attended; the reviewer notes the impact is negligible.
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md and .claude/commands/implement-issue-claude.md: Step 0 session-meta --title call | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The session title is interpolated into a double-quoted shell string, so shell metacharacters in the title could be interpreted as syntax.
  WHY: An operator-set title could theoretically contain a double quote, backtick, or `$(...)`, though the reviewer notes titles normally come from controlled sources.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- .claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py: immediate_block() at f"````text\n{record_example(record)}\n````\n\n" and _occurrence_block() at the same pattern | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The command text from an untrusted session is wrapped in a fixed four-backtick code fence. A command that contains a line of exactly four backticks closes the fence early, allowing the rest of the command to render as unescaped Markdown in the GitHub issue body. A downstream agent or the operator's poller reading the report would see Markdown-formatted text where raw command text was intended.
  WHY: The four-backtick fence is hardcoded and never varies based on content. A permission prompt whose sanitized command happens to contain a four-backtick line will have its fence closed from inside. The fix (variable-length fence via _fenced_text) is planned in issue #5127 whose plan and implement-plan log are in this PR but the code change is not yet applied.
- .claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py: parse_immediate_block() command regex r"^````text\n(.*)\n````$" with re.MULTILINE | re.DOTALL | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The regex uses greedy matching with re.DOTALL. When a command contains a line of four backticks, the .* group captures only up to that internal line instead of the real closing fence, and the remainder of the command sits outside the captured group. lookup then returns a truncated command to the operator's poller.
  WHY: A stuck session whose sanitized command happens to contain a four-backtick line will have its lookup return only the portion before that line, hiding the actual blocking command from the operator. This is the parser side of issue #5127.
- .claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py: _file_pending() reported signature skip | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: _file_pending collects signatures from ALL sessions in _load_immediate_state and skips them regardless of which session reported them. If session A reports pattern X via report-now, session B's separate occurrences of X are skipped by file in session B's stage, and filed-state.json is never updated for session B's occurrences. This undercounts the total occurrences visible in the filed-state.json counter.
  WHY: Two unattended sessions sharing a home directory on a self-hosted runner accumulate occurrences of the same permission-prompt pattern. After the first session reports it, the second session's file silently drops those occurrences. The operator sees a stale "seen N times" count that does not reflect the actual volume.
- .claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py: _report_now() exception handler calling _release_reservation() | severity=high | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: When a POST fails inside _report_now, the except block calls _release_reservation which modifies the in-memory bucket and then tries _save_immediate_state. If _save_immediate_state also fails (disk full, permission error), contextlib.suppress(OSError) swallows the save failure. The in-memory state is updated but the on-disk immediate-state.json retains the pending reservation. The function then raises, which is caught by report_now. On the next report-now call for the same session and signature, sig in bucket["reports"] returns True because the stale pending reservation still exists on disk, permanently blocking any immediate report for that signature in this session.
  WHY: A stuck session hits a permission prompt. The hook spawns report-now. The POST to GitHub fails (network blip). _release_reservation tries to clean up the disk state but also fails (disk full on the runner). The session remains stuck, the operator sees the status_detail but never gets the immediate report. A subsequent prompt with the same signature is also silently not reported. The end-of-stage file still catches it, but the operator waits hours instead of seconds.
- .claude/hooks/permission_prompt_logger.py: spawn_reporter() subprocess.Popen call in main() | severity=low | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The hook now unconditionally spawns a detached child process on every PermissionRequest, with no gating beyond the PermissionRequest event check. The child resolves repo slug via git config, reads environment (CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE_SESSION_ID, CLAUDE_PERMISSION_PROMPT_REPORT), loads local state files, and posts to GitHub. While the kill switch (CLAUDE_PERMISSION_PROMPT_REPORT=off) gates the POST, the process still starts and reads local files before checking the kill switch.
  WHY: In attended sessions (not auto/bypassPermissions mode), a PermissionRequest fires, the hook spawns the child, the child reads the log file and environment, determines the session is attended, and exits without posting. This is by design but wastes a process spawn per prompt in attended sessions. The impact is negligible since permission prompts are infrequent.
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md and .claude/commands/implement-issue-claude.md: Step 0 session-meta --title call | severity=low | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The command files instruct the session to run `permission_prompts.py session-meta --title "<title from get_session>"` with the title interpolated into a double-quoted shell string. If the title from get_session contains a double quote, backtick, or $(...) expression, the shell would interpret it as command syntax rather than literal text.
  WHY: The implement-plan log documents this as accepted under Notes: chain and dispatcher titles are known to never carry shell metacharacters. A title set by an operator could theoretically contain these characters if a stage session's title is user-defined through an edge path, but in practice the titles come from controlled sources (command names, issue numbers, stage labels).
- Requirement: The issue #5127 plan states "Phase 1 — fence the report text so nothing inside can close it ... Done when: the new tests pass against the twin, the rest of tests/test_permission_prompts.py passes except the twin-parity check waiting on the sync, ruff clean"
  Expected change site: workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py should contain _BACKTICK_RUN_RE, _fenced_text(), _CLOSING_FENCE_RE, and updated parse_immediate_block()
  Evidence of absence: The PR diff for workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py is byte-identical to .claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py and contains none of these symbols. The _fenced_text function, _BACKTICK_RUN_RE constant, and _CLOSING_FENCE_RE constant do not appear anywhere in the diff. The implement-plan log for #5127 marks phase 1 as not yet started (checkbox unchecked). The fence fix code was included in the original #4755 plan but the twin-first approach requires it to be committed to workflow-templates/.claude/ separately, which has not occurred on this branch head.

  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
- .claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py: immediate_block(), line 636 — `f"````text\n{record_example(record)}\n````\n\n"`; and parse_immediate_block(), line 887 — `re.search(r"^````text\n(.*)\n````$", section, re.MULTILINE | re.DOTALL)` | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The immediate report wraps the sanitized command in a fixed four-backtick code fence. `record_example` truncates to 2,000 chars and strips heredoc bodies and token-like strings, but does NOT strip backticks. A command containing a line of four or more backticks closes the fence early (per CommonMark closing rule), so the remainder of the command renders as Markdown in the GitHub issue/PR comment that downstream agents and the operator's poller read. The same fixed-fence assumption in `parse_immediate_block` means `lookup` can match the wrong fence and return fields or a command the session never ran.
  WHY: The report text is untrusted session data rendered as Markdown. A session that attempts a command like `echo '````'` or any markdown/grep command containing a four-backtick line escapes the fence, injecting arbitrary Markdown (headings, fake `- **Tool:**` field lines, etc.) into the report. `lookup` then parses that injected text as real fields. This is the exact defect filed by the security audit as `permission-report-markdown-escape` (A03:2021-Injection, medium, confidence 8/10) and trac
